question: A positive progesterone challenge test (withdrawal bleed occurs after progestogen administration) in a woman with amenorrhea indicates that the HPO axis is functioning and the endometrium has been adequately primed by oestrogen.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Progesterone challenge works by adding the final signal (progestogen withdrawal) to an already oestrogen-primed endometrium. A bleed means: outflow is patent, endometrium is intact and oestrogen-primed, and ovaries are producing some oestrogen. The cause of amenorrhea must therefore lie at the hypothalamic/pituitary level (anovulation).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A positive progesterone challenge (withdrawal bleed) requires: (1) an intact outflow tract, (2) a responsive endometrium primed by oestrogen (Compartment 3 intact), and (3) ovarian oestrogen production (Compartment 2 intact). It effectively excludes outflow obstruction, uterine failure, and ovarian failure as the cause of amenorrhea.
